task.title: Multiplication table, sum of evens and vowels
task.description: The platform sets a number n and a word word. 1) With a for loop print 10 lines of the multiplication table for n in the format "5 x 1 = 5" … "5 x 10 = 50" (with a template string). 2) In let evenSum calculate the sum of even numbers from 1 to n inclusive. 3) In let vowelCount count the vowels a, e, i, o, u in word with a for...of loop, ignoring case.

tests.name: Table for 5: 10 lines from "5 x 1 = 5" to "5 x 10 = 50"
tests.check: (() => { const rows = __logs.filter((l) => /^\d+ x \d+ = \d+$/.test(l)); return rows.length === 10 && rows.every((l, idx) => l === `5 x ${idx + 1} = ${5 * (idx + 1)}`); })()
tests.fail: You need exactly 10 lines like `${n} x ${i} = ${n * i}` - spaces around x and =.

tests.name: Table for 7
tests.check: (() => { const rows = __logs.filter((l) => /^\d+ x \d+ = \d+$/.test(l)); return rows.length === 10 && rows.every((l, idx) => l === `7 x ${idx + 1} = ${7 * (idx + 1)}`); })()

tests.name: n = 5: evenSum = 6 (2 + 4)
tests.fail: Accumulator: let evenSum = 0; before the loop, evenSum += i; for even i.

tests.name: n = 10: evenSum = 30
tests.fail: Include n in the range: i <= n.

tests.name: n = 1: evenSum = 0
tests.fail: There are no even numbers from 1 to 1 - the sum is 0.

tests.name: "JavaScript": 3 vowels
tests.fail: Counter: let vowelCount = 0; before the loop, vowelCount++; for vowels.

tests.name: "EDUCATION": 5 vowels (capitals)
tests.fail: Bring the character to lower case: char.toLowerCase().

tests.name: "rhythm": 0 vowels
tests.fail: y is not a vowel in this task; a word without vowels gives 0.

tests.name: A for loop is used
tests.fail: Calculate the table and the sum with for (let i = 1; ...).

tests.name: The program finishes without errors
tests.fail: An error or an infinite loop: check that the loop condition becomes false at some point.

hints: Table: for (let i = 1; i <= 10; i++) { console.log(`${n} x ${i} = ${n * i}`); }
Declare the accumulator and the counter with let BEFORE the loop.
Going through the word: for (const char of word) { ... }

questions.question: How many times does the body of for (let i = 0; i < 5; i++) run? Type a number.
When is the condition checked in for (let i = 1; i <= 3; i++)?
questions.explanation: If the condition is false - the loop ends.

questions.question: What does this print: let sum = 0; for (let i = 1; i <= 4; i++) { sum += i; } console.log(sum);
Match the command with the action.
questions.explanation: break - exit, continue - skip a step.

questions.question: Why is this loop infinite: let i = 1; while (i <= 5) { console.log(i); }
options: i does not change, the condition is always true
while cannot be used with numbers
questions.explanation: Add i++ to the loop body.

questions.question: What goes into char in the loop for (const char of "cat")?
options: The characters c, a, t in turn
questions.explanation: for...of goes through the characters of a string.

questions.question: Where do you declare the accumulator let total = 0;?
questions.explanation: Inside the loop it would reset on every iteration.

questions.question: Match the task with the suitable loop.
pairs: Repeat while the sum is less than 200000
Go through the letters of a word
questions.explanation: The choice depends on whether the number of steps is known.

questions.question: What does this print: let s = ""; for (let i = 0; i < 3; i++) { s += "*"; } console.log(s);
Which numbers does this print: for (let i = 1; i <= 6; i++) { if (i % 3 === 0) { continue; } console.log(i); }
questions.explanation: 3 and 6 are skipped; 5 is printed too, but it is not among the options.

questions.question: Which error does the platform show for an infinite loop?
questions.explanation: The run time is limited, so the loop is stopped.
